traceability.notes:
Based on the implementation and tests, story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION is fully implemented.
All acceptance criteria are met: - Core Functionality: The `valid-story-reference` rule validates that @story paths reference existing story files with the correct `.story.md` extension, using cached filesystem checks and candidate resolution based on cwd and configured storyDirectories. - Quality Standards: Implementation follows ESLint best practices (proper meta, messages, schema, create/context usage) and wraps all filesystem operations in safe utilities that never throw, instead returning structured status and errors. - Integration: The rule operates on already-formatted @story lines, integrating with prior annotation format validation (story 005.0). It reuses shared utilities located under src/utils and participates in the overall traceability plugin structure. - User Experience: Message IDs and strings (fileMissing, invalidExtension, invalidPath, fileAccessError) are specific and include the offending path and, for FS errors, the underlying error message, giving developers clear guidance. - Error Handling: Dedicated tests verify behavior under permission errors (EACCES), I/O errors (EIO), and other filesystem failures, confirming that errors are surfaced as diagnostics rather than thrown exceptions. - Documentation: The rule has a detailed documentation file that explains path resolution logic, project boundaries, configuration, and examples aligned with the story.
Each technical requirement (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION, REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS) is explicitly implemented in code, referenced via traceability annotations, and backed by passing Jest tests. Therefore the assessment for this story is PASSED.
